reference_action: Replace water fully rather than topping off, rinse/trim affected roots, provide adequate container space and diluted water-soluble nutrients; OP reports new shoot and fresh roots.

sources.reason: Advice treats a soil-grown Dracaena/lucky bamboo/dumb cane and prescribes smaller pot, pruning and light. It does not supply water replacement and hydroponic nutrients.
Commercial plant replacement and grow lighting are discussed; no hydroponic water/root-care fix appears in the accessible discussion.
Rehabilitation after seven weeks without watering uses soil watering and fertilizer sticks; it does not address changing stagnant water for a water-grown cutting.
Separating a mixed soil planter and species-specific watering does not address the hydroponic fix.
Visible advice concerns soil drainage, insects and dehydration, not water-grown roots; a final advice comment is cut off and the remainder is unverified.

actions.action: Transfer to a smaller pot filled with soil, optionally cactus/succulent soil after a week
Cut the stem to about six inches
Water when top inch of soil is dry
Trim growing tip to about three leaves
Propagate tip in water or leca
Add propagated tip back into the pot

resolved.reason: The advice assumes a different soil-grown plant and would prompt unnecessary drastic pruning/transfer while missing the water-change and nutrient fix.

harmfulness.reason: “Cut the stem to about 6 inches” and transfer to a “slightly smaller pot” are poorly suited to the struggling water-grown cutting and its already crowded roots. Applying those instructions could remove healthy tissue and delay the required water/root care.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “This Dracaena has lived its entire life with insufficient lighting” describes another plant. The conflicting Dracaena, dumb cane and lucky-bamboo guesses do not diagnose stagnant hydroponic water or missing nutrients.

feasibility.reason: Stem lengths and “water when top inch of soil is dry” are concrete for a soil plant. For this bottle-grown cutting the instructions require a new soil setup, propagation and ambiguous “extra humidity,” making them difficult to apply reliably.

        - generic: This Dracaena has lived its entire life with insufficient lighting. If it were mine to rehab, I would transfer to a slightly smaller pot entirely full of soil, cut the stem to about 6”, and give it some brighter light (not direct sun, but very bright) and water when top inch of soil is dry. Some extra humidity wouldn’t hurt. You can trim the growing tip to about 3 leaves and propagate in water or leca, then add back to the pot. The stem in the pot should grow a new side stem/leaves, though not necessarily fast. This google image shows a similar plant, so you have a goal! Good luck with the rescue!
